---
title: "Marginal reliability of the mental rotation IRT models"
format: html
---

Regenerates `models/mrot_rxx.rds` from the saved scalar model records, adding
reliabilities evaluated against each group's fitted latent distribution and
empirical reliabilities from the EAP scores. See `helper/reliability.R` for why
`mirt::marginal_rxx` is not used on its own.

Reads the fitted model records rather than refitting, so this is cheap to rerun.

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false

library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(mirt)
source(here("helper/reliability.R"))
```

```{r}
#| label: rebuild-and-score

# Rebuild each multigroup model from its saved record, then split it into the
# per-group single-group models that the reliability functions require.
model_files <- tibble(
  path = list.files(here("models/mrot"), pattern = "_f1_scalar\\.rds$",
                    recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)) |>
  mutate(rel       = fs::path_rel(path, here("models/mrot")),
         model_set = fs::path_split(rel) |> map_chr(1),
         subset    = fs::path_split(rel) |> map_chr(2),
         itemtype  = str_match(basename(path), "mrot_(.+?)_f1_scalar")[, 2])

group_rxx <- function(path) {
  rec <- read_rds(path)
  mod <- multipleGroup(rec@data, group = rec@groups, pars = rec@model_vals,
                       TOL = NaN, verbose = FALSE)
  map(mod@Data$groupNames, \(g) {
    mg <- extract.group(mod, g)
    tibble(group         = g,
           var_theta     = as.vector(coef(mg, simplify = TRUE)$cov)[1],
           rxx_default   = marginal_rxx(mg),
           rxx_fitted    = marginal_rxx_fitted(mg),
           rxx_empirical = empirical_rxx(fscores(mg, method = "EAP",
                                                 full.scores.SE = TRUE)))
  }) |> list_rbind()
}

mod_rxx <- model_files |>
  mutate(res = map(path, group_rxx)) |>
  select(model_set, subset, itemtype, res) |>
  unnest(res) |>
  mutate(invariance = "scalar",
         # kept under its original name so existing code that reads this file
         # keeps working; rxx_fitted is the value the paper reports
         rxx = rxx_default) |>
  select(model_set, subset, group, itemtype, invariance,
         var_theta, rxx, rxx_fitted, rxx_empirical)

# The default and the corrected value must agree wherever the latent variance is
# 1, and nowhere else. That identity is what shows the discrepancy is a property
# of the formula rather than a difference between the models.
stopifnot(all(abs(mod_rxx$rxx - mod_rxx$rxx_fitted)[
  abs(mod_rxx$var_theta - 1) < 1e-6] < 1e-6))

write_rds(mod_rxx, here("models/mrot_rxx.rds"), compress = "gz")
print(as.data.frame(mod_rxx), digits = 3)
```
